- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on B&O Railroad in this auction.

I have $668 and no monopolies. p1 has $824 but needs Tennessee to complete orange and Illinois to complete red. p2 owns St Charles, Illinois, Pennsylvania Ave, and Boardwalk.

p4 has $270 cash and a brown monopoly with hotels. They already own Reading and Pennsylvania RR. If they win B&O, they would have three railroads for $100 each in rent. That is more than their current cash.

Short Line is still unowned. A lone railroad is too weak to justify a large bid. I must keep p4 from owning three railroads. I need to cover Tennessee denial and Marvin Gardens without overspending.

A bid around $150 to $200 would deny p4 their third railroad without overpaying. p2 and p1 may also bid to block p4. The list price is $200.

p2 is unlikely to bid $200. A lone railroad is worth only $50 to $100 to me because Short Line remains unowned. Denying p4 a third railroad is the real strategic value, since their rent would jump from $50 to $100 per landing. I should bid modestly to force p4 to pay up, but I will take the property if it stays cheap.

p4 cannot build more hotels on browns. They will likely bid aggressively for the third railroad to raise their rent from $50 to $100. I must keep $668 intact. I need $180 to deny p1 Tennessee and $280 for Marvin Gardens.

Reserving both Tennessee and Marvin leaves only $208 in cash. Boardwalk is owned by p2, so dark blue cannot be completed from the bank. I will bid incrementally to block p4 from winning cheap without revealing a ceiling. The current high bid is zero.

I will open the auction at the minimum bid of $1 to probe interest. p4 wants the property and may raise quickly, while p2 started it and might not care. I will keep raising incrementally without showing a ceiling.

A lone railroad is worth roughly $80 to $120, and blocking p4's third railroad adds another $50 to $100. That puts the fair bid around $150 to $180. Cash is not the binding constraint until bids reach that level.

p2 refused the $200 list price, signaling they do not value the property at that level. Paying the full list would leave only $468 in cash, which is enough to cover Tennessee and most of Marvin, but it may still be overpaying.

I will bid $1 to probe interest without appearing desperate. I will keep raising incrementally and never reveal a ceiling. I will not help p4 acquire Short Line either.
